title: De Stijl
summary: Black lines, white planes, and blocks of red, yellow, and blue. Only horizontals and verticals.
lede: The Dutch movement around the journal *De Stijl* (1917–1931) and Mondrian’s neoplasticism: compositions built only from horizontal and vertical lines and rectangular planes, in the three primary colors and the three non-colors black, white, and gray, balanced by asymmetry instead of symmetry.

era.note: From the first issue of the journal to Theo van Doesburg’s death. The look continues in later revivals, often as a “Mondrian” pattern.

lineage.label: Cubism
lineage.note: Wikidata (P737) and Wikipedia name Cubist painting as an influence. Mondrian’s grids of about 1914–1916 grew out of Cubist work in Paris.

lineage.label: Neoplasticism
lineage.note: Mondrian’s theory, first named in the journal in 1917. Tate treats it as the name for the art that the De Stijl circle practised, so this record uses it as an alias for the core of the style.

lineage.label: Elementarism
lineage.note: Van Doesburg’s later branch (from about 1924) that admits diagonals. Tate and Wikipedia record that Mondrian left the group over it. This record covers the orthogonal core and treats diagonal work as this branch.
Van Doesburg taught informal De Stijl courses in Weimar in 1921–1922, and Wikipedia states that De Stijl influenced the Bauhaus style.

lineage.label: Constructivism
lineage.note: Wikidata (P737) and Wikipedia record that Malevich and Russian Constructivism influenced the group after about 1921.

grammar.text: Straight black lines of equal or varied weight divide the surface into rectangles. There are no curves and, in the core style, no diagonals.

Red, yellow, and blue as flat, unmixed planes, with black, white, and gray. Mondrian’s paintings of 1920–1921 use several whites and grays and some solid black planes. White and gray usually cover most of the surface.
Planes of unequal size balance by opposition: a large colored plane against small ones in the far corners. Lines run to the edge of the field or stop just short of it.
No modelling, texture, shadow, or gradient. In furniture and buildings, planes and bars overlap without joining, each one painted in its own color.
Blocky sans-serif letters built from straight strokes, as in van Doesburg’s 1919 alphabet. Capitals and letter-spaced titles are common.
Pure abstraction. Nothing is depicted. Color and proportion carry the whole composition.

diagnostic: Every line and edge is horizontal or vertical.
Thick black lines divide the surface into rectangles.
Flat red, yellow, and blue planes sit among larger white or gray planes.
The composition is asymmetric but balanced.
counter: Diagonals as the main structure (that is Elementarism or Constructivism).
Secondary or pastel colors such as green, orange, purple, or pink.

confusions.difference: Bauhaus uses circles, triangles, and diagonals and often lowercase type. De Stijl uses only rectangles and straight horizontal and vertical lines.
The Swiss style uses the grid invisibly and relies on type, often with one accent color. De Stijl makes the grid visible as thick black lines and fills cells with primary colors.
Neo-brutalism also uses thick black outlines and bright fills, but adds hard offset shadows, rounded corners, and pastel or secondary colors.
Constructivism is built on diagonals, red and black, and photomontage. De Stijl is orthogonal and does not use images.
Memphis clashes many colors, patterns, and irregular shapes. De Stijl keeps three primaries and three non-colors in plain rectangles.

do: Build the layout as a visible grid: thick black lines between rectangular cells.
Use flat red, yellow, and blue for a few cells. Keep most cells white or light gray.
Make the balance asymmetric: one large colored plane, and smaller ones in the opposite corners.
Use a condensed or square sans-serif in capitals for headings.
Let lines run through to the edge of the container.
dont: Do not use rounded corners, circles, or curved shapes.
Do not use diagonals, rotation, or skew.
Do not use green, orange, purple, or tints of the primaries.
Do not use gradients, shadows, textures, or photographs.

synthesis: Mondrian’s paintings of 1920–1921 set the core grammar: a [white center ringed by black, gray, and primary planes](ref:mondrian-composition-yellow-red-black-blue-gray-1920), or [one large blue plane answered by small red, black, and yellow ones](ref:mondrian-composition-large-blue-plane-1921). The primaries in both are less pure than later pastiche, and gray and black cover as much area as color.

Van Doesburg shows the range of the movement. His [Composition XXII](ref:van-doesburg-composition-xxii-1922) drops the black lines and uses ochre and gray-green; his [1917 windows](ref:van-doesburg-stained-glass-composition-iv-1917) are dense mirrored patterns with green and brown glass; the [Aubette ciné-dancing](ref:aubette-cine-dancing-strasbourg) turns the grid 45°, which is Elementarism. The black line grid is Mondrian’s signature more than a rule of the whole group.

Type and print follow the same rule: van Doesburg’s [alphabet](ref:van-doesburg-alphabet-1919) and [Section d’Or poster design](ref:van-doesburg-section-dor-poster-design-1920) build letters from right angles only, and the [journal cover and advertisements](ref:de-stijl-journal-cover-and-advertisements-1922) use black capitals, one red, vertical text, and thick black bars as frames.

In three dimensions the planes separate: the [Schröder House](ref:rietveld-schroder-house) and the [Red Blue Chair](ref:rietveld-red-blue-chair) use primaries as thin bars or single boards against white, gray, and black, and [Café De Unie](ref:cafe-de-unie-rotterdam) makes a facade into a graphic panel with lettering.

Websites in the style are rare. Of about 25 candidates checked on 28 September 2026, one is a clear example, a small student page on [Neocities](ref:destijl-neocities-website) whose header is a Mondrian grid. Four are borderline: the [Van Doesburghuis](ref:vandoesburghuis-website) uses flat primary panels without black lines, the [Mondriaanhuis](ref:mondriaanhuis-website) uses offset line frames and yellow, [Mondrian Generator](ref:mondriangenerator-com-website) draws compositions as images beside square outlined controls, and the [100 jaar De Stijl](ref:100jaardestijl-website-2021) holding page has only a rectilinear logo. No kept site passes the fingerprint.

The fingerprint is therefore not calibrated on real sites. The main blind spot is the line: web imitations draw black bars as filled boxes or grid gaps, so `surface.border.medianWidth` reads 1 px, and generators draw the composition in a canvas that computed styles cannot see. Judge such pages by the rubric.

fingerprint.note: Positive marker. Thick black lines divide the planes; other catalogue styles use 3 px or less. Provisional: set from the specimen, recalibrate with measured references. Checked on 28 September 2026: every kept website capture measures 1–3 px or none, because web imitations draw the black lines as filled boxes or grid gaps, not CSS borders ([destijl.neocities.org](ref:destijl-neocities-website) shows about 24 px bars and measures 1 px). The range is unchanged; judge such pages by the rubric.
Positive marker. Red, yellow, and blue all appear, and no fourth hue family. Provisional: set from the specimen, recalibrate with measured references.

Positive marker. The primaries fill real planes, but white and gray planes cover more of the surface. Provisional: set from the specimen, recalibrate with measured references. Stored painting images measure 0.18 ([1920](ref:mondrian-composition-yellow-red-black-blue-gray-1920)) and 0.41 ([1921](ref:mondrian-composition-large-blue-plane-1921)), inside the range.

Positive marker. Headings, labels, and navigation are set in capitals, after the rectilinear capitals of the journal and van Doesburg’s alphabet. Provisional: set from the specimen, recalibrate with measured references. Supported by the journal cover, the alphabet, and the poster design; only 1 of 5 kept website captures ([Mondriaanhuis](ref:mondriaanhuis-website)) reaches it. Unchanged, because the one clear website example is a small student page.

tokens.$description: Authored tokens for de-stijl. Shorthand values; tools/build.mjs writes DTCG 2025.10.

bg.$description: Off-white ground, like Mondrian’s painted whites.

surface.$description: Pure white planes set against the ground.

subtle.$description: Light gray plane: gray is one of the three non-colors.

muted.$description: Mid gray: secondary text, and the darker gray plane.

references.title: 100 jaar De Stijl placeholder page
references.note: Borderline: the logo follows van Doesburg’s rectilinear alphabet and the primary palette, but the rest of the page is a plain centered holding page.

references.title: Alphabet in “Stijl letters”
references.note: The rubric’s rectilinear capitals at their source: every letter is made from horizontal and vertical strokes only.

references.title: Café De Unie, Rotterdam
references.note: De Stijl applied to a commercial front: flat rectangles in primaries, black, and white, with lettering built into the composition.

references.title: Ciné-dancing, Aubette, Strasbourg
references.note: Partial fit, Elementarism: flat primaries, gray, and white in rectangular panels, but the main structure is diagonal, the branch the style record treats as related, not core.

references.title: Composition with Large Blue Plane, Red, Black, Yellow, and Gray
references.note: A textbook neoplastic composition: one dominant primary plane, small opposing color planes at the far edges, gray and white fields, and black lines that stop short of some edges.

references.title: Composition with Yellow, Red, Black, Blue, and Gray
references.note: A canonical neoplastic painting of 1920: only horizontal and vertical lines, flat primaries with black, white, and several grays, and an asymmetric balance around a white center.

references.title: Composition XXII
references.note: Partial fit: orthogonal flat planes in an asymmetric balance, but without the black dividing lines, and with an ochre yellow and a gray-green that are not in Mondrian’s strict palette.

references.title: De Stijl journal cover and advertisement page, 1922
references.note: The movement’s own journal: rectilinear sans-serif capitals, one flat primary, text turned vertical, and thick black bars as structure.

references.title: De Stijl student site on Neocities
references.note: Clear in the header: black horizontal and vertical bars that run off the edge, with flat red, yellow, and blue planes among white ones. The body below is plain text, and the page describes the movement as well as using it.

references.title: Design for a poster for La Section d’Or
references.note: Partial fit: the typography is fully orthogonal, in van Doesburg’s rectilinear letters, but the sheet is black on paper with no primary colors.

references.title: Mondriaanhuis website
references.note: Borderline: the logo and photographs are framed by offset black horizontal and vertical lines, and the buttons are flat yellow, but the lines are thin, photographs dominate, and there is no red or blue plane.

references.title: Mondrian Generator (mondriangenerator.com)
references.note: Borderline: the page exists to produce the style, and its controls use square black-outlined boxes and flat yellow and black, but the composition itself is a generated image and the page chrome uses thin outlines.

references.title: Red Blue Chair
references.note: The movement’s best-known object: separate bars and boards that overlap without joining, each painted one color, in the primaries and black.

references.title: Rietveld Schröder House, Utrecht
references.note: The movement’s best-known building: planes and bars that overlap without joining, white and gray surfaces, and small primary accents.

references.title: Stained-Glass Composition IV
references.note: Partial fit: an early De Stijl work that is strictly orthogonal and built from flat colored rectangles, but uses green, ochre, and brown glass and a mirrored, near-symmetric layout that the mature style drops.

references.title: Van Doesburghuis website
references.note: Borderline: flat primary panels with square corners, but no black dividing lines, a bright sky blue instead of a primary blue, lowercase type, and a photograph.
